text:
olivia (PM): Quick sync — launch checklist for embeddings endpoint. Need final decisions on batching limits, embedding dims, model variants, and response shape. Targeting GA in ~3 weeks. Thoughts?

ramon (eng-ml): +1. For batching: do we expose item-based limit (e.g. 1000 vectors) or token-based (e.g. 4096 tokens)? Runtime handles dynamic batches up to 4096 tokens today but SLOs vary.

sasha (eng-platform): From infra POV: latency SLO is 95th < 120ms for single-item realtime. Allowing huge item batches will explode tail. Suggest default max_batch_size: 256 and max_batch_tokens: 4096. Offer explicit "bulk" path for larger jobs.

kevin (product): Customers (search/indexing) ask for very large throughput. Proposal: two tiers — realtime default (sync) with max_batch_size=256, and bulk async (up to 10k items) with callback/signed-URL. Keep API ergonomics simple.

olivia (PM): Dims: many customers want 1536 for quality, others want 768 for cost. Can we support both sizes at launch? Also need to decide canonical response: full JSON arrays vs compressed binary (base64/gzip).

ramon (eng-ml): Runtime already has optimized kernels for 768 and 1536 quantized checkpoints. We can serve both, but it doubles model variants stored and index footprint. Recommend shipping 1536 as default (better quality) and 768 as "lite".

sasha (eng-platform): Naming/variants: propose 'redwood-embed-large-v1' (1536) and 'redwood-embed-small-v1' (768). Routing policy: default -> large, but customers can request small for cost. Also include model metadata in response (model id + dim).

kevin (product): Response format discussion: keep simple JSON list of floats per item for up to 256 results. For bulk, returning huge JSON is unwieldy. Options: (A) gzip + application/json; (B) base64-encoded float32 bytes in JSON; (C) signed URL to compressed ndjson or .npy. Which one do users prefer?

ramon (eng-ml): My vote: (1) Default realtime: JSON arrays of floats (widest compatibility). (2) Bulk async: return signed URL to a compressed float32 blob (npy or gzipped ndjson). SDKs can parse automatically. Example realtime response: 

```json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-large-v1",
  "usage": { "items": 3 },
  "data": [
    { "id": "0", "embedding": [0.001, -0.23, ...] },
    { "id": "1", "embedding": [0.12, 0.04, ...] },
    { "id": "2", "embedding": [0.5, -0.1, ...] }
  ]
}
```

Bulk async example: 

```json
{
  "status": "accepted",
  "job_id": "abc123",
  "result_url": "https://s3.redwood.internal/emb-results/abc123.npy.gz",
  "format": "float32_npy_gz",
  "model": "redwood-embed-large-v1"
}
```

kevin (product): That looks good. We should include a small helper in SDKs to return floats instead of base64 bytes. Also add an explicit field for vector_dim to avoid mistakes.

olivia (PM): Launch criteria (proposed): docs + quickstart, examples for both realtime and bulk, SDK support for parsing both formats, perf tests (95th <120ms single-item realtime; measured throughput for 256 batch), canary on dedicated infra with top 5 customers, and model quality eval (embedding retrieval A/B vs current baseline). Any objections?

kevin (product): No objections. Add a migration note for customers who relied on previous embeddings format (if any) and a guide for switching dims. Also add evals for embedding-quality on few retrieval datasets.

sasha (eng-platform): Ops items: default rate-limit for realtime = 60 req/min/key, separate quota for bulk jobs. We'll need telemetry: sample payload sizes, average batch_size, per-model p95 latency. Also we should expose per-route cost estimate in console.

infra-bot: Deploy scheduled to canary pool on 2025-09-08T19:00:00Z — will announce when canary passes.

olivia (PM): I'll update the PRD and open RFC capturing these choices and the launch checklist. Assigning @ramon for runtime changelist, @sasha for infra and rate-limiting, @kevin for docs/SDKs and evals. Thanks everyone :rocket:
